narrative.overview:
CatOrder looks like a 1920s-30s Felix the Cat cartoon turned into a wayfinding sign: ink on paper, round shapes, thick outlines, and exactly one question on screen at a time. The customer's own words sit on top, the order is a plain list below them, and a single black band pinned to the bottom asks the next decision. The cat logo is the only picture in the product.

Everything is two-tone. Ink and paper carry every surface, and the cat's green eyes appear only where the person should look. Titan One speaks (names, questions, numbers); Rubik reads (everything else).
keyCharacteristics: Ink on paper; one green accent reserved for "look here".
One black decision band, fixed at the bottom, asking one question.
Titan One for names, questions and numbers; Rubik for text.
Round forms: pills, discs, soft-cornered buttons, a 24% rounded logo with an ink outline.
Flat: depth comes from inversion (black against white), never from shadow.
Large type for a counter-side read: 24px body, 40px question, 64px number.

rules.name: The Look-Here Rule
rules.body: Green marks the one thing to look at: asked words, the matching line, the live dot. If two things are green and they are not the same question, one is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: Every surface is ink or paper. Grey is for text only, never for surfaces or borders.

rules.name: The Speak/Read Rule
rules.body: Titan One is for what the product says or counts; Rubik is for what the customer said and what is listed. Never set running text in Titan One, and never set it in bold synthesis (font-synthesis is off).

rules.name: The Outline-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A thing that floats gets a 2.5px ink outline and a paper fill. A thing that matters gets an ink fill.

dos: Do keep every surface ink or paper; use grey only for text.
Do use Cat-Eye Green only to mark where to look, always under ink text.
Do ask one question at a time in the band, in Titan One, with white answer buttons.
Do outline floating or quiet controls at 2.5px ink; fill the ones that matter with ink.
Do keep touch targets at 44px or more (60px on the band).
Do keep the logo the only picture; the customer's photo is content, not decoration.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, blurs or a second accent color.
Don't use green for buttons, borders, icons or decoration.
Don't set running text in Titan One, or fake its bold.
Don't build a three-column inbox/message/order layout or a chat thread.
Don't add a second persistent bar or a modal for decisions; the band is the only place the product asks.
Don't show a guess as fact: doubt is a question in the band.
